ledger.summary: Beyond Bourton Abbas Ralph crosses a dry waste and enters the Wood Perilous on a ridge: first beech, then a stately oak forest with deer. At a crossroads he falls asleep and is seized by about two hundred men of the Burg of the Four Friths under Sir Aymer, with five bound prisoners wearing the leafless tree. Old Oliver recognises Ralph's gear and knows Nicholas; a runner brings news and the company rides off south-east, leaving Ralph.
ledger.geography_notes: From the dale's brow beyond Bourton Abbas: a rough dry waste fit only for mountain sheep and goats, then a long ridge covered with unbroken wood (the Wood Perilous). A highway pierces it: beech first, then well-spaced oaks with greensward. A crossroads where the ground falls to a little dale with holly and thorn. The Burg company rides off south-east, slantwise of the crossroads. Ralph says Upmeads is "beyond the down country".
